providers.title: Basic identities of cubic Gauss sums
providers.scope: |G(a)| = mu^2(a); G(ab) = conj(chi_b(a)) G(a) G(b) for coprime primary a, b; G(conj a) = conj G(a).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Kummer's sums
providers.scope: For p = 1 mod 3 and a primary prime pi with pi conj(pi) = p, G(pi) + G(conj pi) = S_p/sqrt(p), so S_p/(2 sqrt p) = Re G(pi).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The cube of a Gauss sum
providers.scope: G(pi)^3 = -pi/|pi| for every primary prime pi: by Jacobi sums for split primes, by a coset decomposition for inert primes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Patterson's first moment
providers.scope: The sum of G(pi) over primary primes of norm at most X is (6/5) c_* X^(5/6)/log X + o(X^(5/6)/log X). Proved in the seventh lesson, using the named results N1 to N3.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The rational form
providers.scope: The sum of S_p/(2 sqrt p) over primes p <= X is (3/5) c_* X^(5/6)/log X + o(X^(5/6)/log X), half the coefficient of the sum over primary primes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The ordinary character large sieve
providers.scope: For primitive characters modulo primary squarefree moduli of norm at most Q and coefficients of length Z, the square sum is at most a constant times (Z + Q^2) times the coefficient norm, with no power of Q lost.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Extensions of the cubic large sieve
providers.scope: Heath-Brown's cubic large sieve (named result N1) extended to inner coefficients that are not squarefree and to outer variables over all of Z[omega], at the cost of X^epsilon.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The functional equation for Q(omega)
providers.scope: For a primitive Hecke character of conductor norm D and angular order l, the completion (sqrt(3D)/(2 pi))^s Gamma(s + |l|/2) L(s) satisfies a functional equation with a root number of absolute value 1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Type I comparison
providers.scope: For outer length R << X^0.51, the Type I sums of G minus the model, in a fixed angular mode, are O(X^(5/6 - 1/100)). Uses the level Voronoi formula (named result N2) and the cubic large sieve.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Type I sums at large heights
providers.scope: The mean over heights |t| ~ T of the twisted Type I sums is O(X^(1/2 + epsilon) R^(3/4) T^(1/2)), from the level formula alone.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Exceptional character moments
providers.scope: For convolutions of smoothly weighted prime sequences, the square sums over coprime squarefree p, q near the configurations (Y, 1) and (Y^(1/3), Y^(1/3)) save a fixed power over Y^(7/3).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Corrected dispersion
providers.scope: After subtracting the model c_* conj(G(a)) N(a)^(-1/6) S(u), the second moment over a of the bilinear form in b is O(Q L^(-K)); the frequencies that are cubes produce exactly the square of the model.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The constant of the cube frequencies
providers.scope: For a radial weight W, the integral of the transform of W at z^3 equals c_*^2 times the integral of W(y) |y|^(-2/3).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Prime decomposition
providers.scope: The prime sum is an exact combination of L^O(1) Type I and bilinear sums with independent coefficients, the same for the Gauss sums and the model; only products of three primes near X^(1/3) escape a power saving.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The dyadic comparison
providers.scope: For every fixed angular order l, the sum over X < N(pi) <= 2X of theta_l(pi)(G(pi) - c_* N(pi)^(-1/6)) is o(X^(5/6)/log X); with l = 0 this proves Theorem 4.1 of the first lesson.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Fixed powers
providers.scope: For every fixed k not divisible by 3, the sum of G(pi)^k over N(pi) <= X is the main term of the first moment for k = 1 and k = -1, and o(X^(5/6)/log X) otherwise.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
